title: Hard to start when cold
h1: Why is my car hard to start when it's cold?
metaDesc: Car hard to start on cold mornings? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's the battery, fuel pressure, sensors or glow plugs, and how urgent it is.
synonyms: car hard to start in the morning
car hard to start in cold weather
takes a long time to start in the morning
car struggles to start in the cold
car starts after several tries in the morning
intro: Cold weather is hard on batteries, thickens engine oil and makes engines need more fuel to start. That's why a weak part often shows up first on a cold morning. Answer the questions below to see whether it's the battery, the fuel system or something else, and what to do next.
safety: If you smell raw fuel, stop trying to start it and keep sparks and flames away.
Don't warm the car up in a closed or attached garage. Exhaust fumes can build up quickly.
Don't crank for more than 10 seconds at a time. Wait about a minute between tries.

q_what_happens.q: What happens when you try to start it cold?
q_what_happens.help: "Cranking" is the whirring sound of the engine turning over (rrr-rrr-rrr) before it fires up.

opts.a: It cranks slowly and sluggishly, like it's struggling
Rapid clicking, or nothing at all
It cranks at normal speed but takes a long time to fire up
It starts, but shakes, runs rough or stalls until it warms up
It's a diesel and it cranks a long time, often with white smoke

q_battery.q: Which of these fits your battery?
q_battery.help: The battery's date is often on a sticker or stamped on top. If you can't find it, choose "I'm not sure".

opts.a: It's newer, but the battery light has come on or the lights dim while driving
It's newer and tests fine, with no warning lights
I smell raw fuel, or see a wet spot under the car
It starts much better if I turn the key to ON for a few seconds before cranking
The check engine light is on, or it runs rough after it starts
None of these / I'm not sure

result.title: The battery may be too weak for cold starts
result.now: Check that the battery clamps are tight and free of crusty buildup, then have the battery tested. Many auto parts stores test batteries free.
if: If it fails a load test, replace it before it leaves you stranded. Age alone doesn't prove it's bad, but a battery older than about 4 to 5 years is worth testing before winter.

If it won't start at all, a jump start or booster pack may get you going. If you jump-start it, follow your owner's manual. Don't jump a battery that is cracked, leaking, swollen or smells like rotten eggs.
If the battery tests good, ask them to test the alternator and starter too.
If the battery light comes on or the lights dim while driving, the charging system may be the problem. Have it tested soon.
result.why: A battery loses a lot of its strength in the cold, while cold, thick oil makes the engine harder to turn. An aging battery that seems fine in summer often can't keep up on a cold morning.

causes.name: Aging or weak battery
causes.clues: The battery is more than 4 years old, and the crank has gotten slower over time.

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery terminals
causes.clues: White or green buildup on the clamps.

causes.name: Battery not getting fully charged
causes.clues: Mostly short trips, or the car sits for days at a time.

you: Check and clean the battery terminals.

result.title: The alternator may not be keeping the battery charged
result.now: Get the charging system tested within the next few days. Until then, avoid short trips with lots of lights and accessories on.
if: If the battery light comes on and stays on while driving, the car may run only until the battery is drained. Head for a safe place to stop rather than a long drive.
If the headlights get dim and the dash flickers, pull over safely. The battery is running out.
If the battery light comes on along with a rising temperature gauge or heavy steering, a broken drive belt is possible. Pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: A newer battery that keeps running low usually isn't getting recharged properly. Cold weather makes the problem show up first because starting takes more power.

causes.name: Failing alternator
causes.clues: The battery light flickers or stays on, or the lights dim at idle.

causes.name: Loose or worn drive belt
causes.clues: A squeal on startup, especially when cold or damp.

causes.name: Something draining the battery while parked
causes.clues: It's worst after the car sits overnight or for a few days.

you: Watch for the battery light while driving.
Listen for a belt squeal on startup.

result.title: A worn starter, poor cable connection or too-thick oil are possible causes
result.now: Check your owner's manual or the oil cap for the correct oil grade and compare it with your last oil change receipt. Then book a check of the starter and cables.
if: If the crank keeps getting slower or you hear grinding, get it checked soon. A starter that's failing usually gets worse.
If the battery cables feel warm after cranking, a poor connection is likely. Tell the shop.
If you smell burning or see smoke from under the hood after cranking, stop trying to start it.
result.why: With a good battery, a slow cold crank points to something resisting the starter or limiting its power. A worn starter, a corroded cable or ground strap, or oil that's thicker than recommended can each do it.

causes.name: Worn starter motor
causes.clues: The crank is slow even when warm, or it has made grinding noises.

causes.name: Corroded cable or loose ground strap
causes.clues: Visible corrosion, or a cable that's warm after cranking.

causes.name: Engine oil that's too thick for the weather
causes.clues: A recent oil change with a different grade than the manual lists.

you: Check the oil grade used at the last oil change.
Look for corrosion on the battery cables and ground strap.
shop: Voltage-drop test on the battery cables

result.title: Fuel pressure may be draining away overnight
result.now: Turn the key to ON and wait a few seconds before cranking, or do it twice, to let the fuel pump build pressure. Book a check when convenient.
if: If it starts getting harder to start even with this trick, or it hesitates while driving, get it checked sooner.
If you smell fuel at any point, stop trying to start it and have it inspected before driving.
result.why: The fuel system is meant to hold pressure after you shut off the engine. If a valve in the pump or a leaky injector lets it bleed off overnight, the pump has to refill the lines before the engine can start, so it cranks longer.

causes.name: Leaking check valve in the fuel pump
causes.clues: Long crank after sitting for hours, but quick restarts after short stops.

causes.name: Leaking fuel injector
causes.clues: A puff of black smoke on startup, or a fuel smell.

causes.name: Weak fuel pump
causes.clues: Hesitation under hard acceleration too.

you: Turn the key to ON and listen for the pump's 2-second hum from the back.
Note whether pre-priming makes it start quickly.

result.title: A sensor or ignition problem may be making cold starts harder
result.now: Have the trouble codes read, then book a check. Many parts stores read codes free.
if: If the check engine light is flashing, don't drive it. That usually signals a serious misfire that can damage the catalytic converter.
If it stalls while driving, don't drive it until it's fixed.
result.why: A cold engine needs extra fuel and a strong spark to start. For example, if the coolant temperature sensor tells the computer the engine is warm, it won't add that extra fuel. Worn spark plugs or weak coils also struggle most in the cold.

causes.name: Faulty coolant temperature sensor
causes.clues: The temperature gauge acts oddly, or the engine runs rich or lean when cold.

causes.name: Worn spark plugs or weak ignition coil
causes.clues: Rough running or a misfire code, especially on damp mornings.

causes.name: Dirty throttle body or vacuum leak
causes.clues: A low or uneven idle after it starts.

you: Get the codes read and write them down.
Check when the spark plugs were last replaced.
shop: Code scan and live coolant temperature data

result.title: The engine may not be getting the right mix when cold
result.now: Let it idle for 30 seconds before driving off on cold mornings, and book a check when convenient.
if: If the check engine light flashes or the car shakes hard, don't drive it. A misfire can damage the catalytic converter.
If it stalls once you're moving, don't drive it until it's checked. Losing the engine can make steering and braking much harder.
If you smell fuel, stop the engine and keep sparks and flames away.
result.why: A cold engine needs a higher idle and extra fuel until it warms up. If a temperature sensor reads wrong, the idle system is dirty, or a cylinder misfires in the cold, the engine shakes or dies until it warms.

causes.name: Dirty throttle body or idle control fault
causes.clues: A low, uneven idle that improves when warm.

causes.name: Faulty coolant temperature sensor
causes.clues: The temperature gauge acts oddly, or fuel economy has dropped.

causes.name: Cold misfire from worn plugs or a weak coil
causes.clues: Shaking or a flashing check engine light right after starting.

causes.name: Vacuum leak
causes.clues: A hissing sound, or an idle that smooths out when warm.

you: Note the outside temperature when it happens.
Watch for a flashing check engine light.
shop: Code scan and live sensor data

result.title: Diesel cold starts often point to glow plugs or the battery
result.now: Turn the key to ON and wait for the coil-shaped glow plug light to go out before cranking. If it's still hard to start, book a check of the glow plugs and battery.
if: If the glow plug light flashes or stays on while driving, have the system scanned soon.
If it's very cold and the fuel looks cloudy or the engine starts then dies, the fuel may be gelling. Use a block heater if you have one and get it checked.
result.why: Diesel engines rely on glow plugs to warm the cylinders before a cold start. If some have failed, or the battery can't power them and the starter together, the engine cranks a long time and puffs white smoke until it catches.

causes.name: Failed glow plugs or glow plug controller
causes.clues: A long crank with white smoke that clears once it's running.
causes.against: If it starts fine with a long glow wait, a weak battery is more likely.

causes.name: Weak battery
causes.clues: A slow crank, or the battery is more than 4 years old.

causes.name: Fuel gelling in extreme cold
causes.clues: Very cold temperatures, and it starts then dies or loses power.

you: Wait for the glow plug light to go out before cranking.
shop: Glow plug resistance and circuit test
Fuel filter and fuel condition check

result.title: Possible fuel leak. Stop trying to start it
result.now: Don't try to start it again. Keep sparks and flames away and have the car towed.
if: If fuel is dripping or pooling, move people away from the car and call the fire department.
If the smell fades and you can't see a wet spot, still have it checked before starting again. Fuel can leak where you can't see it.
result.why: A raw fuel smell or a wet spot can mean fuel is getting somewhere it shouldn't. A leak can also let fuel pressure drain away overnight, which causes long cranking, and fuel near hot parts is a fire risk.

causes.name: Leaking fuel line or fitting
causes.clues: A wet spot under the car along the fuel line route.

causes.name: Leaking injector seal or fuel rail
causes.clues: The smell is strongest at the engine.

causes.name: Flooded engine from repeated tries
causes.clues: Several long cranking attempts, and no visible leak.

you: From a distance, look for drips or wet spots under the car.
Don't smoke or use flames nearby.

result.title: Start with a battery test, then a shop check
result.now: Have the battery tested, since it's one of the most common causes of hard cold starts. If it passes, book a shop check and describe exactly what you hear.
if: If you smell fuel, stop trying to start it and keep sparks and flames away.
If it won't start at all, a jump start is a reasonable first try. If you jump-start it, follow your owner's manual. Don't jump a battery that is cracked, leaking, swollen or smells like rotten eggs.
If the check engine light flashes or the engine shakes hard after starting, don't drive it.
result.why: Hard cold starts come from three main areas: battery and starter, fuel delivery, and the sensors that set the cold-start fuel mix. The battery is the easiest and most common place to start.

causes.name: Weak battery
causes.clues: A slow crank, or the battery is more than 4 years old.

causes.name: Fuel pressure loss overnight
causes.clues: A normal crank that takes a long time to fire.

causes.name: Sensor or ignition problem
causes.clues: A check engine light, or rough running when cold.

you: Record a short video with sound of a cold start. It helps the shop a lot.
